question: The Commission communication entitled ‘Roadmap towards Nature Credits’, published on 7 July 2025, states that: ‘Nature credits can be a key tool to reward nature-positive action through private investment to the benefit of both nature and businesses’.

Furthermore, on page 8, it is stated: ‘A range of pilot projects across the EU and beyond are already testing real-world approaches to nature credits, generating essential experience to guide future policy and practice’.

More specifically, on the same page, the communication states that one of these pilot projects in located in Peru: ‘Outside the EU, a project in Peru is assessing how EU-based companies can contribute to biodiversity conservation abroad while meeting EU sustainability reporting standards’. 1.

The Carbon Removals Certification Framework Regulation ((EU) 2024/3012) is limited to removal activities within the EU. Has the Commission made any decision yet as to whether it will also limit any EU certification framework of ‘nature-positive activities’ to activities within the EU?

Does the Commission intend to include or certify ‘nature-positive actions’ or nature credits implemented in non-EU countries in any future EU nature credit certification or governance framework that it might propose?
If so, has the Commission considered that such projects in non-EU countries would have severely negative consequences for the land and resource rights of local and indigenous communities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.12.2025) The Roadmap towards Nature Credits1 sets out a stepwise, exploratory process to examine how high-integrity nature credits could complement public funding in rewarding naturepositive action. This preparatory work focuses primarily on the EU context, while reflecting the international dimension under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework2.

In parallel, under the Regulation on Carbon Removals and Carbon Farming (CRCF)3, the Commission will develop methodologies for the certification of carbon farming activities, including their biodiversity co-benefits. The Commission will take stock of existing evidence to assess the need for scaling up nature credit markets.

The Roadmap refers to a range of pilots within and beyond the EU, designed to test practical approaches and gather evidence. One of them is carried out in Peru4 with local authorities and partners. It examines how EU-based companies may support nature-positive action abroad.

The Roadmap stresses that all work must ensure transparency, integrity and social safeguards, and that knowledge and practices by Indigenous Peoples and local communities must be meaningfully included, with full respect for their rights, knowledge systems, and roles as stewards of biodiversity.

This approach shaped the pilot project in Peru, involving Peruvian communities and indigenous people from the outset to identify enabling conditions for responsible, high-integrity biodiversity finance.

1 https://ec.europa.eu/newsroom/env/items/892839/. 2 https://www.cbd.int/gbf. 3 https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/carbon-removals-and-carbon-farming_en. 4 The Peru Pilot is one concrete action deriving from the Letter of Intent signed at the COP16 between the
Commission and the Peruvian Government. More information on the pilot in the National Park Sierra del Divisor.
